summary.text: 喜 is traditionally analyzed as 壴, an upright drum, above 口. A proposed drum-and-singing interpretation motivates its association with joy, though the strokes alone do not establish that scene.

formation.text: A semantic compound in the traditional analysis: 壴 contributes a drum image, while 口 contributes the idea of singing. The resulting drum-and-singing or music-making scene is a proposed motivation for joy; another interpretation links the graph to hearing drum music or setting up a drum for a festive event. These interpretations do not establish a sequence of meanings.

components.text: 壴 is identified as an early picture of an upright drum, with a top ornament, face, and support. Here it contributes the drum image; the evidence does not establish a phonetic role in 喜.
口 is the mouth element in the traditional analysis. In the proposed drum-and-singing explanation, it contributes the idea of singing rather than depicting a mouth as part of a literal scene.

history.text: Oracle-bone and bronze forms are reported with 壴 above 口. Later recorded categories include Chu manuscript, small-seal, and Shuowen forms. The selected oracle-style and seal-style illustrations are modern redrawings; they show script styles but do not establish a sequence of graphic changes.
Shuowen analyzes 喜 as formed from 壴 and 口 and glosses it as joy. This is an early lexicographic explanation, not independent confirmation of the proposed drum-and-mouth motivation.
憙 is a separate graph that was later sometimes conflated with 喜. 歖 is reported as an ancient-script form of 喜; the available account does not establish a fuller graphic sequence.

uncertainties.text: The drum-and-singing account is one proposed motivation. Other interpretations connect the graph with hearing drum music and smiling, or setting up a drum for a festive event. No dated chain connects these proposals to particular forms or meanings.

Reported oracle-bone examples include joy or rejoicing and name uses, but the examples are not individually dated well enough to establish which came first. Bronze evidence also includes music terminology and a ritual use read 喜(饎); its relation to ordinary joy is unresolved.
Modern summaries include “like,” “love,” and “enjoy,” but the supplied historical account does not date these uses or establish their development from joy.
壴 is not established as a phonetic element in 喜. The supplied historical readings offer no clear sound match, and modern readings alone cannot prove an ancient phonetic role.

senses.text: Oracle-bone examples are reported with the meaning joy or rejoicing. Name uses are also reported in this corpus, so the evidence does not establish which attested use came first.
Personal and polity-name uses are reported among oracle-bone examples; their priority relative to joy or rejoicing is unresolved.

The evidence does not establish semantic connections among joy, the bronze music term, the ritual reading, and later glosses such as “like” or “love.”

items.period: Shang oracle-script style; the file page gives a Sinica source label J11924 and note 戩45.7 合23607 but no absolute date for this individual form
items.caption: An oracle-script style form of 喜 places a branched upper shape above a rounded lower enclosure. The upper shape is analyzed as 壴, an upright drum graph, and the lower as 口; the proposed drum-and-singing motivation is an interpretation, not a meaning visible in the strokes.
items.alt: Black oracle-script style character with a tall branched upper part and a rounded lower enclosure containing a short horizontal stroke.
items.selection_reason: This redraw gives a useful visual example of an oracle-script style form alongside the reported 壴-and-口 analysis. The component interpretation and its proposed association with joy remain scholarly explanations.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; no absolute date assigned to this redraw
items.caption: A small-seal style form of 喜 has a branched upper shape above two enclosed sections. Shuowen analyzes 喜 as formed from 壴 and 口, but that lexicographic account does not independently confirm the proposed drum-and-singing motivation.
items.alt: Black small-seal style character with a branched top, a rounded middle enclosure, and a broad lower enclosure.
items.selection_reason: This distinct script-style example complements the oracle-style form and illustrates a later recorded category. The redraw does not establish a dated sequence of graphic changes.

limitations.text: The drum-and-singing account is a proposed explanation of the graph’s motivation. Other interpretations have been offered, and oracle-bone examples are reported with both joy and name uses without secure dates establishing their order.
These illustrations are modern redrawings of script styles, not photographs of inscribed objects. Their script labels do not establish a dated sequence of forms.
